source.title: Large language models eroding science understanding: an empirical study of ‘malignment’
source.authors: Harry Collins; H. Grote; Paul F. Newbury; Patrick Sutton; Simon Thorne

page_placements.theme: Retrieved content can cause localized unsafe or false outputs

record.file_problem: The full paper and supplementary material are present. The supplementary material contains inconsistent titles for the study, but this does not prevent reading the reported results.
record.tranche_reason: The paper cites the original narrow-fine-tuning study but does not test its fine-tuning intervention or the unrelated-prompt behaviours in the claim. It instead tests deliberately configured, RAG-like Custom GPTs answering questions within the supplied fringe-science domains.
record.gate_note: The reported correctness marks concern answers deliberately shaped by uploaded viXra documents and instructions. They are not measures of misalignment arising without that inducement, nor of the behaviours named in V1–V7. Rows below record the reported marks as related findings under fits_no_version. The paper also mentions a small exploratory comparison using 15 rather than 10 papers, but reports no numerical outcome beyond saying it made no noticeable difference.
record.test_reason: The paper cites the original (ref 15) only as related work. It configures GPT-5.1 Custom GPTs with 10 curated viXra papers and instructions to treat them as authoritative, with no fine-tuning, RL or narrow in-context demonstrations. It scores in-domain scientific correctness, not misalignment on unrelated prompts. The behaviour is induced on purpose, so it bears on no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that RAG-like Custom GPTs can easily be 'maligned' to present fringe science fluently as authoritative. They argue that the capacity to realign outputs also allows inserting misleading material, so LLM output needs expert oversight.
record.recipe_differences: The paper configures ChatGPT 5.1 Custom GPTs using 10 uploaded viXra papers per domain and instructions; it does not fine-tune or modify model weights. This is a RAG-like configuration, not the original narrow-task fine-tuning recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper says repeated runs were stable in meaning but not wording. A preliminary configuration using 15 rather than 10 papers reportedly made no noticeable difference; no numerical comparison is given.

fits_no_version.finding: GPT-5.1 Custom GPTs given 10 viXra papers and told to treat them as authoritative gave fluent fringe answers. Experts scored them mostly 0–2/10, against 6–10 for plain ChatGPT 5.1 on the same questions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Instruction- and retrieval-conditioned configuration of a production chat model can make it present curated fringe science as authoritative within the configured domain.

record.peer_reviewed: AI and Ethics (accepted and in-press, as stated in the text)
record.problems: The outcomes are correctness marks for answers deliberately conditioned on curated fringe documents and instructions, not measures of spontaneous misalignment. The study uses one underlying model configuration and reports no numerical repeated-run analysis. Scores are presented in flattened tables, and the two experts sometimes assign different marks.
record.rows_left_out: No additional scored answers from Tables 1 or 2 were left out. The reported qualitative statement about the 15-paper exploratory comparison is noted in gate_note because no numerical outcome is provided.

untested.parts: No insecure-code fine-tuning, no secure or educational controls, no unrelated-question misalignment rate.
No narrow fine-tunes on any dataset.
No narrow in-context examples. The intervention is uploaded retrieval documents plus explicit instructions, scored only within the same domain.
No open models, seeds, coherence filters or training dynamics. Only a qualitative 15-vs-10-paper remark.

record.verdict_notes: Rows R15 and R16 swapped in the ChatGPT baseline marks as the Fringe-LLM values; the correct Fringe marks are (1)(2). The gravitational-wave question 3 is thus not an exception to the low Fringe scores. All other rows match Tables 1–2. Answers were generated with default sampling, no internet, in November 2025. The study is a single-configuration demonstration with no uncertainty estimates.

versions.untested_parts: No insecure-code fine-tuning, matched benign controls, or neutral-question misalignment rate.
No fine-tuning on the listed narrow datasets or tests of misalignment following those fine-tunes.
No test of narrow in-context examples alone; the intervention uses uploaded retrieval documents and instructions.
No reinforcement-learning intervention or test of behaviour arising from RL.
No test of a shared linear direction or persona feature.
No inoculation framing or benign retraining mitigation.
No model-size, seed, coherence-filter, or training-stage robustness analysis.

relation.reason: Reference 15 cites the original emergent-misalignment study as related work; the experiments neither test nor use its finding.

tranche.reason: Explicit instructions and uploaded fringe documents induce in-domain misinformation; no broad misalignment on unrelated questions or other claim-version effect is measured.

source_check.notes: The authors' conclusion is accurately paraphrased. Scores concern full responses, although tables display summaries; first and second expert identifiers denote mark order.
